deflected-amsb-singlet-vectorlike-messen.reason: Stored one-generation/non-MSSM sector is incomplete. Source Sec. II inherits the MSSM; messenger species and multiplicities must be selected from a definite source benchmark. Table II fixes NF=N5+3N10=10, not a unique (N5,N10). The displayed SU(5) component hypercharge/conjugation conventions also require resolution. Do not invent missing fields.

problems.rationale: The U(1)_H extension is explicitly analyzed as a massless down-quark solution to the strong CP problem, with its non-invertible symmetry protecting the down-type Yukawa matrix.

evidence.quote: For this reason, such models inform us about massless down-quark solutions to the strong CP problem.

problems.rationale: The SU(3)_H extension is explicitly developed as a massless down-quark solution to strong CP, using the non-invertible Peccei–Quinn symmetry to protect the down Yukawa.

evidence.quote: when the non-invertible $\mathbb{Z}_{3}^{\bar{d}}$ Peccei-Quinn symmetry is preserved there are massless quarks and CP is a symmetry of the strong sector of the SM.

mechanisms.rationale: The model explicitly identifies the non-invertible symmetry protecting massless down quarks as a Peccei–Quinn symmetry tied to the strong-CP solution.

evidence.quote: the non-invertible $\mathbb{Z}_{3}^{\bar{d}}$ Peccei-Quinn symmetry is preserved

problems.rationale: The paper uses curvature-induced heavy-lifting of the SM Higgs scale to test electroweak naturalness and explicitly characterizes the SM as having a hierarchy problem.

evidence.quote: If the heavy-lifted gauge theory suffers a hierarchy problem, such as does the Standard Model, confirming such predictions would demonstrate a striking violation of the Naturalness Principle.
Since this NMSM clearly suffers from a hierarchy problem (worse than the SM), the precision NG measurements would therefore provide us with a test of “un-naturalness” in Nature

mechanisms.rationale: The SM Higgs vacuum expectation value breaks the gauge symmetry and sets the gauge-Higgs masses; during inflation the curvature term raises the symmetry-breaking scale.

evidence.quote: for c > 0, the symmetry breaking scale setting gauge-Higgs physical masses is naturally of order H.

problems.rationale: The paper analyzes an MSSM benchmark in this scenario, explicitly reporting that its spectrum satisfies the dark matter relic requirement.

evidence.quote: such a spectrum can satisfy the dark matter relic requirement

mechanisms.rationale: The analyzed MSSM spectrum includes the Higgs sector and its electroweak mass spectrum, with soft parameters and the 125 GeV Higgs mass explicitly analyzed.

evidence.quote: a viable soft SUSY spectrum and the 125 GeV Higgs boson mass can be obtained

problems.rationale: The paper presents gauged scale symmetry as a possible solution to the Higgs hierarchy problem and analyzes its protection of the Higgs mass in SMW.

evidence.quote: could give a solution to the hierarchy problem
could give a solution to the hierarchy problem

mechanisms.rationale: The model specifies Weyl gauge symmetry breaking in which the Weyl vector obtains mass by absorbing the scalar mode extracted from the curvature-squared term.

evidence.quote: By a Stueckelberg breaking mechanism, ωμ has become a massive Proca field, after “eating” in (ST) the derivative ∂μ ln φ of the Stueckelberg field ln φ

mechanisms.rationale: The Higgs potential and vacuum expectation value break electroweak symmetry and generate masses for the electroweak gauge bosons.

evidence.quote: The EW symmetry is thus broken at tree level.
the EW scale ⟨σ⟩ and Higgs mass are

problems.rationale: The paper explicitly presents the sterile-neutrino extension as accounting for active-neutrino mass hierarchy through the seesaw mechanism.

evidence.quote: Through the additional mass and interaction terms, sterile neutrinos can account for the mass hierarchy among active neutrinos via the seesaw mechanism

mechanisms.rationale: The Lagrangian specifies gauge-singlet sterile neutrinos with a Yukawa coupling to the SM lepton and Higgs fields and a Majorana mass term; the paper connects these terms to active-neutrino masses through the seesaw mechanism.

evidence.quote: y_{\alpha i}\,\overline{L}_\alpha\,\widetilde H\,N_i + \frac{1}{2}\,\overline{N}_i^{\,c}\,(M_N)_{ij}\,N_j
sterile neutrinos can account for the mass hierarchy among active neutrinos via the seesaw mechanism

mechanisms.rationale: The SM Higgs is localized on the TeV boundary, where its vacuum expectation value gives the W and Z their observed masses and deforms their zero-mode wave functions.

evidence.quote: the Higgs field which must be localized on the TeV boundary in order for the $W$ and the $Z$ gauge bosons to get their observed masses
The effects are the result of the deformation of the $Z$ and $W$ zero-mode wave-functions due to the presence of the Higgs filed in the low energy boundary.

problems.rationale: The paper explicitly considers whether hidden-sector dark matter would be millicharged in this model and concludes it would not; it does not specify a dark-matter candidate or abundance mechanism.

evidence.quote: the hidden sector dark matter if it exists would not receive a milli-charge

mechanisms.rationale: The model includes a Stueckelberg mass term and a gauge-invariant vector–compensator combination for the added U(1)_X gauge field.

evidence.quote: \bar C_\mu=C_\mu+ \partial_\mu \sigma/M_1 is the combination of C and the axion field \sigma which is gauge invariant under the U(1)_X gauge transformation

problems.rationale: The model assigns a residual Z2 symmetry that stabilizes the lightest portal-sector particle and analyzes its production and propagation as highly boosted dark matter.

evidence.quote: The Z_2 symmetry makes the lightest one of φ_i, ψ stable, and allows it to be dark matter.
the highly-boosted dark matter whose energy originates from the cosmogenic neutrinos

problems.rationale: The paper treats the ultralight dark photon as a dark-matter candidate and derives bounds on that candidate using Galactic Center gas clouds.

evidence.quote: In this work we place new bounds on ultra light dark photon dark matter for m ≤ 10⁻¹⁰ eV.
Ultra-light dark photon dark matter is a plausible dark matter candidate

mechanisms.rationale: The stated dark-photon mass may be generated by the Stueckelberg mechanism; the paper explicitly identifies that mass-generation option for this model.

evidence.quote: The mass m of the dark photon can be generated via the Stückelberg mechanism for simplicity

problems.rationale: The paper studies the millicharged particle as a possible fraction of dark matter and projects sensitivity to the millicharged SIDM window.

evidence.quote: MCP in our parameter of interest can account for a fraction of the dark matter (DM) abundance
FORMOSA can help cover a large part of the millicharged DM region that is previously unconstrained.

problems.rationale: The paper tests the first KK mode of the hypercharge gauge boson as a dark-matter candidate by calculating its resonant annihilation and thermal relic abundance against WMAP.

evidence.quote: The first KK mode of $B$ boson, $B^{(1)}$, is a viable dark matter candidate by virtue of KK-parity.
We now calculate the thermal relic density of the LKP dark matter using annihilation cross section obtained in Sec. \ref{sec:cross_section}.

mechanisms.rationale: The model’s thermal relic abundance is evaluated using the freeze-out annihilation rate and Boltzmann evolution; the paper identifies thermal decoupling and computes the resulting abundance.

evidence.quote: It is important to evaluate the thermal average of the cross section at the freeze-out temperature because it affects the calculation of the abundance of the thermal relic.
In case of the UED model the LKP decouples from thermal equilibrium at $T \sim m/25$.

problems.rationale: The paper tests a specified departure from standard charge assignments and constrains its parameter using charge conservation and matter neutrality.

evidence.quote: The present experimental limits on the masses of νμ and ντ are 270 keV and 35 MeV respectively, so it is not impossible to invalidate the bounds in Eqs. (17)-(18) and in Eq. (21).
experiments on the neutrality of atoms places a bound given by |ε| < 10^{-21} on the allowed non-standard electric charges Q_st + ε (L_e - L_μ)
